methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 9 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Standard Electron, a Seed-stage Climate & Energy company founded by Tyler Norwood and Alex Le Roux, has raised approximately $3.2M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable in the climate and energy sector, including companies like Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the Climate & Energy sector—fewer than three datapoints satisfied narrow filtering criteria. Consequently, the valuation relies on a stage-progression methodology. Applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to the next financing round to the $3.2M raised as a valuation proxy yields an $8M implied value.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $7M to $9M, centered at $8M. This range reflects the single applicable method and carries material uncertainty given the narrow peer set at this stage. Key sensitivities include the appropriateness of the 2.5x multiplier for this specific subsector, the timing and terms of the next funding round, and the company's progress against technical and market milestones between now and that round. Additional comparable transactions and clearer metrics on product development would strengthen future valuations.
